changes.before: Change Session s{12} to Session s{7}. What does duration return?
changes.after: Give an object's members their starting values with a constructor.

before: A constructor has the class name and no return type. It runs when an object is created. The : minutes{n} member initializer initializes minutes before the constructor body.

explicit prevents this one-argument constructor being used as an implicit conversion. Session s{12} deliberately constructs a Session. int minutes has no separate default initialization here: the initializer supplies it.
Members initialize in their declaration order, not the order you type in the initializer list. Use initializers for members, especially const or reference members that cannot be assigned later.

Expected output or behavior: 12
. Local compiler test evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Add a second int member with its own constructor parameter and print both values. You may trace this without a compiler; finishing the reading is not proof of a local run.
after: A constructor sets up a new object. It has the same name as its class and no return type. Creating s calls the Session constructor.
The part after the colon, minutes{n}, gives minutes its starting value. This happens before the constructor body runs. The body is empty because the initializer already does the needed setup.
explicit stops this constructor from silently converting an int into a Session. Session s{12} deliberately asks to create a Session using twelve.
The program prints 12. The constructor stores twelve in minutes, and duration() reads that value.
When a class has several members, they initialize in the order they are declared in the class. Reordering the constructor's initializer list does not change that order.
